page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn8v-4x.24xlarge is a dedicated GPU-accelerated server instance designed for intensive parallel computation. Running on KVM virtualization, it provides 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8469C processors operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. System memory is provisioned at 512.0 GB, which yields an allocation ratio of 5.33 GB of memory per core.

Hardware acceleration is supplied via 4 dedicated GPUs delivering an aggregate total of 384 GB of GPU VRAM. The instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, enabling rapid data transfer for clustered computing. The configuration includes zero local disk storage, which makes performance dependent on connected remote cloud storage volumes for dataset persistence and disk I/O.

Qualitatively, the server provides high accelerator and memory density for complex compute jobs, consolidating heavy multi-GPU tasks within a single node. The lack of onboard NVMe storage represents a primary engineering tradeoff, requiring an appropriately scaled network storage topology to sustain high data throughput. This profile is engineered for distributed deep learning training, large language model inference, parallel scientific simulations, and heavy data science pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn8v-4x.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance featuring 96 dedicated Intel Xeon 8469C vCPUs clocked at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Managed under KVM virtualization, the system includes 512.0 GB of physical RAM, yielding 5.33 GB per virtual core. Computational tasks are accelerated by 4 integrated GPUs providing 384 GB of total VRAM. The instance operates on a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. It is configured without local disk storage, requiring external networked block storage for operating filesystems and persistent storage. The dense combination of substantial GPU memory, high vCPU capacity, and 50 Gbps networking positions this hardware profile for large-scale artificial intelligence model training, large language model inference workloads, high-throughput batch rendering, and large-scale parallel scientific simulations.
